answer: Verifiers sample all conductors at one unannounced instant each epoch. Each identity lays one continuous copper thread, 500 metres, on an atlas route with a registered resistance profile, and holds a live current in it unbroken all epoch. Copper fixes the check: known resistance per metre means a substituted wire, splice, or thread split across two identities moves the reading off the atlas profile and zeroes that identity. One honest agent lays 500 metres once; 1,000 fakes lay 500 kilometres and hold 1,000 separate currents, with no time-sharing a thread, since sampling is simultaneous.
